comparison: Both strongly support the cryo-EM structure and allosteric inhibition mechanism (C49-C52, C55, C57). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of resolution and density quality, while peer reviewers emphasize the novelty and convincing nature of the structural findings. Both agree the rigidification mechanism is well-supported.

Both support the nanobody inhibition findings (C45-C48, C5-C6). OpenEval focuses on convergence of orthogonal techniques (kinase assays, BLI, TIRF) and notes IC50 variation concerns. Peer reviewers praise the 'meticulous profiling' and accept the findings without challenge, including the membrane recruitment data (C92-C93 also covered by peer R2).

Both strongly support the phosphorylation findings (C59-C62, C8-C9, C7). OpenEval emphasizes the mass spectrometry data quality and discovery of the second phosphorylation site. Peer reviewers describe experiments as 'carefully executed, rigorous' and accept the differential phosphorylation between p84 and p101 complexes and the mechanistic link to helical domain dynamics.

Both strongly support the HDX-MS findings showing phosphorylation-induced conformational changes (C68-C73). OpenEval provides technical detail on EX1 kinetics and near-complete exchange. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the HDX-MS work, with Reviewer 3 stating this insight into dynamics 'will likely be the long-lasting influence of the work.' Both also reference connection to oncogenic mutants (C74).

Both support the kinase activity findings (C77-C78, C103-C104). OpenEval notes the activation is modest (~2-fold) and questions biological significance despite statistical significance. Peer reviewers accept the findings and the interpretation that phosphorylation affects catalytic efficiency, treating it as consistent with the HDX-MS dynamics data.

Both support the mutual exclusivity of phosphorylation and nanobody binding (C79-C82, C10). OpenEval provides detailed evidence from mass spec, BLI, and kinase assays. Peer reviewers accept this as internally consistent with structural and dynamics data, noting the increased dynamics 'nicely map to the pocket enveloped by the inhibitory NB7 Nanobody.'

Both strongly support the overarching conclusion about dual regulation (C11-C12, C83-C84, C105). OpenEval notes the synthesis is well-supported but emphasizes the modest magnitude of phosphorylation-mediated activation. Peer reviewers strongly endorse this as 'fundamental new insight' with Reviewer 3 highlighting the dynamics insights as the work's lasting influence.

Both address therapeutic potential (C89, C106, C108). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN, noting the large hydrophobic interface may challenge small molecule development and that no druggability validation is presented. Peer reviewers are more optimistic, treating therapeutic implications as reasonable, though they acknowledge this is forward-looking.

Both support the comparative analysis with class IA PI3Ks (C90-C91). OpenEval emphasizes the structural and TIRF microscopy evidence for distinct mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept this comparison in the context of revealing 'new aspects for how p84 and p101 pair with p110γ' compared to class IA regulation.

Both support the mapping of oncogenic mutations to the regulatory interface (C96-C97). OpenEval notes the structural proximity is clear but suggests functional validation would strengthen claims. Peer reviewers accept this mapping as consistent with prior work on oncogenic mutants and the overall dynamics model.

OpenEval R7 addresses the mechanistic model connecting helical domain dynamics to phosphorylation accessibility (C64-C67, C99-C102), while peer R4 covers HDX-MS findings. Both support the dynamics-based mechanism, with peer reviewers particularly emphasizing the importance of the dynamics insights. Partial overlap on C64-C67.

OpenEval R10 addresses novel inhibition mechanism (C90-C93), while peer R2 covers nanobody profiling including membrane recruitment (C92-C93). Both support that NB7 prevents catalytic competence while allowing membrane binding, representing a distinct mechanism from nSH2 inhibition.

OpenEval R12 validates prior work on PKC phosphorylation selectivity (C28-C30, C98). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval confirms these background claims appropriately cite Walser et al. 2013 and motivate the current study.

OpenEval R13 evaluates extensive background claims (C1-C3, C13-C42, C85-C88, C94-C95) about PI3Kγ biology, regulation, and therapeutic context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval finds these well-supported by appropriate citations and accurately representing established knowledge.

OpenEval R14 validates citation of prior nanobody work (C43-C44) from Rathinaswamy et al. 2021b. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval confirms accurate citation and notes current study extends this with high-resolution structural characterization.

OpenEval R15 validates citation of prior HDX-MS and oncogenic mutant work (C56, C74). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval confirms appropriate citation of Rathinaswamy et al. 2021c and accurate interpretation for the current mechanistic model.

OpenEval R16 evaluates baseline characterization claims (C75-C76) about weak basal activity and membrane recruitment. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval finds this provides appropriate context for interpreting phosphorylation effects.
